claims.text: 21 RCTs, 8,805 participants with acute bacterial conjunctivitis; all treatments topical
claims.quote: We included 21 eligible RCTs, 10 of which were newly identified in this update. A total of 8805 participants were randomized. All treatments were topical in the form of drops or ointment.

claims.text: antibiotics likely improved clinical cure by 26% (RR 1.26; 95% CI 1.09 to 1.46; 5 trials, 1,474 participants; moderate certainty)
claims.quote: antibiotics likely improved clinical cure (resolution of clinical symptoms or signs) by 26% (RR 1.26, 95% CI 1.09 to 1.46; 5 trials, 1474 participants; moderate certainty) as compared with placebo.

claims.text: 55.5% placebo vs 68.2% antibiotic clinical resolution by days 4 to 9
claims.quote: In the placebo group, 55.5% (408/735) of participants had spontaneous clinical resolution by days 4 to 9 versus 68.2% (504/739) of participants treated with an antibiotic.

claims.text: microbiological cure RR 1.53 (95% CI 1.34 to 1.74; 10 trials, 2,827 participants) among culture-positive participants
claims.quote: antibiotics likely increased microbiological cure (RR 1.53, 95% CI 1.34 to 1.74; 10 trials, 2827 participants) compared with placebo at the end of therapy

claims.text: authors describe a modestly improved chance of resolution
claims.quote: the use of topical antibiotics is associated with a modestly improved chance of resolution in comparison to the use of placebo.

claims.text: no serious systemic side effects; non-fluoroquinolones linked to more ocular side effects (RR 4.05), very low certainty
claims.quote: There was no evidence of serious systemic side effects ... FQs (RR 0.70 ...) but not non-FQs (RR 4.05, 95% CI 1.36 to 12.00) may result in fewer participants with ocular side effects ... very low certainty.

claims.text: acute conjunctivitis affects about 6 million people a year in the US

claims.text: hyperacute: severe copious purulent discharge, decreased vision, high risk of corneal perforation; treatment intramuscular ceftriaxone
